statement.p: Find the gradient of the function f(x,y,z) = y^{2}\ln\mathopen{}\left(zx\right), at the point (e,-1,1)

static.solution: f_x=y^{2}\frac{1}{zx}z, f_y=2y\ln\mathopen{}\left(zx\right) and f_z =y^{2}\frac{1}{zx}x. Thus \mbox{grad} f = \frac{y^{2}\cdot 1}{zx}z\,\mathit{\vec i}+2y\ln\mathopen{}\left(zx\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+\frac{y^{2}\cdot 1}{zx}x\,\mathit{\vec k} and \nabla f(e,-1,1) = 0.367879\,\mathit{\vec i}-2\,\mathit{\vec j}+\,\mathit{\vec k}.
